summary: Sandstorm functions as a personal server platform designed to host various self-hosted applications with a focus on isolation and security. It acts as an umbrella environment where you can install and run web apps through a unified interface. The codebase is implemented primarily in C++ and Shell scripts.
goodFor: It suits technical users who want to trial multiple isolated self-hosted applications on a single machine without configuring separate containers for each one.
watchOut: The project exhibits low development activity and lacks recent tagged releases, meaning you may encounter unresolved bugs or security vulnerabilities without timely patches.
deployNotes: Given the C++ and shell-based implementation, you will typically need a dedicated Linux environment with persistent storage volumes configured for the underlying application data.
